problem: What is the remainder when ${x}^{4}+2{x}^{3}-1$ is divided by ${x}^{2}+1?$

feedback.problem: What is the remainder when ${x}^{4}+{x}^{2}+2$ is divided by ${x}^{2}+x+1?$
feedback.worked_solution:
Notice that the dividend is missing the ${x}^{3}$ and $x$ terms. So, we first rewrite it by including the missing terms with zero coefficients, as follows:

$$
{x}^{4}+{x}^{2}+2={x}^{4}+0{x}^{3}+{x}^{2}+0x+2
$$

Now, using the method of polynomial division, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,\,\,\,{x}^{2}-x+1 \\  & {x}^{2}+x+1\,\enclose{longdiv}{\,\,{x}^{4}+0{x}^{3}+{x}^{2}+0x+2\,\,} \\  & \,\,\,\,\,{{x}^{4}+{x}^{3}+{x}^{2}}_{―} \\  & \,\,\,\,\,-{x}^{3}+0{x}^{2}+0x+2 \\  & \,\,\,\,\,\,{-\,{x}^{3}-{x}^{2}-x}_{―} \\  & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,{x}^{2}+x+2 \\  & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,{{x}^{2}+x+1}_{―} \\  & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

- the quotient is ${x}^{2}-x+1,$ and

- the remainder is $1.$
